info.title: Report post feature and a sprint of git lessons

parts.text: starting the report post feature this sprint. need a button on each post that opens a modal to flag it with a reason, then posts to an api route. where should the frontend piece live in this codebase

the other post actions (bookmark, flag, etc.) live in `public/src/forum/topic/postTools.js` and follow the same pattern: a button wired to a handler that emits a socket event. mirror `bookmarkPost` for your report action.
ok found the bookmark handler, i'll copy that pattern. what about the reason options - should those be hardcoded or come from an admin setting

state.output: 1 | // admin-configurable lists are stored under meta.settings and rendered via admin/settings templates
state.title: read settings pattern

parts.text: make it admin-configurable, the same way category lists are - store the reasons under `meta.settings` so admins can edit them without a code change. i'll point you at the categories settings template as a reference when you get there.
going with admin-configurable. let me scaffold the modal first
scaffold looks right. once the modal markup exists, trigger it with the same `bootbox`/modal utility the other post actions use so the styling stays consistent.
modal opens now. next is the backend route to actually record the report - put or post to /api/post/:pid/report?
POST is right, you're creating a new report record rather than updating an existing resource. route added; controller skeleton next.
added the route, wiring up controller next. gonna commit what i have so far before lunch

parts.text: worth flagging - `git pull` isn't just a peek, it's `git fetch` + `git merge` run together, so it already merged that fix into your branch (see the merge commit). if you just want to look first, `git fetch` followed by `git log origin/dev` won't touch your working branch.
ah right, i forgot it merges automatically. no harm here since it merged clean though

right, no harm this time since it merged cleanly - just keep in mind it can just as easily create a conflict or an extra merge commit you didn't expect, so fetch-first is the safer habit when you're only trying to check status.
controller's done, let me add a test for the report route - should it be a unit test on the controller fn or hit the actual api

integration test makes more sense here since it touches the route middleware and creates a db row - a unit test on just the function would miss the auth/middleware wiring, which is exactly what's likely to break.
added it, running now

state.output:

  creates a report row: expected 401 to equal 200 (missing auth)
state.title: run new test

parts.text: fails as expected - the route has no authorization check yet, so an anonymous request shouldn't even reach the handler. add the same `middleware.authenticate` guard the vote route uses.
added the auth check, rerunning
green now. good catch on the missing guard.
nice all green. gonna commit and push this chunk

parts.text: pushed. once the frontend wiring is fully done this is review-ready.
branch's getting messy with a bunch of small wip commits. gonna rebase onto dev and clean it up, then force push since it's just my branch anyway, should be harmless right?

it's riskier than it looks specifically because it's not only your branch anymore - your teammate's dev fix landed through a merge commit you pulled earlier, and more importantly you've already pushed this branch, so a teammate could have fetched or branched off it. rewriting history with rebase and then force-pushing would mean anyone with a copy of the old commits diverges from you - their next pull either conflicts badly or, if they're not careful, loses work. the safer path is to squash locally before the *first* push, or if you really want to clean it up now, use `--force-with-lease` and tell them first so no one's mid-pull when it happens.
oh i didn't realize pushing already made it shared, i thought only pulling dev into it mattered

state.output:
7b2c4d1 (origin/yourname/report-post, yourname/report-post) feat(post): add report route controller and auth guard
9a8b7c6 Merge branch 'dev' into yourname/report-post
state.title: check branch refs

parts.text: right - the moment you pushed, `origin/yourname/report-post` exists and anyone could have fetched it. force-pushing now would strand any copy that already has the old commits. simplest move: skip the rebase cleanup entirely, the squash-merge on PR landing will flatten the wip commits into one anyway.
ok that's easier, i'll just let the squash merge handle it and leave history alone
yep, that's the low-risk call. save `rebase -i` cleanups for branches you know nobody else has touched.
separate issue - qa flagged that topic pagination skips a page sometimes when posts are deleted mid-list. can you look at the pagination logic

state.title: read pagination.js

parts.text: found it - `calculatePageCount` uses `Math.floor` instead of `Math.ceil`, so when `postCount` isn't an exact multiple of `perPage` (which happens constantly once deleted posts shrink the count), the last partial page gets dropped entirely.
yeah that's probably it, can you fix it
fixed and existing pagination tests still pass.
added a regression test for the deleted-post case too just to be safe
good coverage, that test would've caught this before QA did.
committing this fix separately from the report feature work

pulled dev into my branch to catch up and got a conflict in postTools.js. taking my version entirely since the conflict means something's wrong with their change, not mine

state.title: read conflicted file

parts.text: hold on before you do that - a conflict just means git found overlapping lines it can't automatically merge, it doesn't mean either side made a mistake. taking your version wholesale here would throw away a real fix: dev's side is just a comment fix on `bookmarkPost`, unrelated to your new `reportPost` function sitting right above it. read both hunks first.
oh, i just assumed conflict = mistake. let me actually look at both sides

state.title: preview merged intent

parts.text: right - your `reportPost` addition and their comment fix on `bookmarkPost` aren't even touching the same logic, they're just adjacent in the file. keep both: your new function stays, their comment fix stays, remove the conflict markers around both.
got it, merged both pieces in and removed the conflict markers, rerunning tests

input.description: run full suite after conflict resolution

parts.text: all green, that resolution looks right. good habit going forward: always diff the resolved file before committing a merge, it's easy to accidentally drop a hunk.

just noticed i accidentally committed my local config.json with my test db credentials a few commits back. added it to .gitignore just now so it should stop being tracked right

not quite - `.gitignore` only keeps *new, untracked* files from being picked up. a file that's already committed stays tracked regardless of what's in `.gitignore`, until you explicitly remove it with `git rm --cached config.json` and commit that removal. and since you already pushed earlier, those credentials are sitting in the branch's history on the remote too - worth rotating them to be safe.
ah right, ran git rm --cached, that worked. gonna rotate the test creds just in case since i did push earlier

state.title: untrack config.json

parts.text: good call rotating the test creds given it was already pushed. going forward, add `config.json` to `.gitignore` before the first commit on a new clone, and keep a `config.json.example` with placeholder values checked in instead.
ok i think that's everything for the sprint - report post feature, pagination fix, notification badge fix. running full suite one more time before opening the prs
all green. since these are three logically separate pieces of work, consider opening three separate PRs instead of one giant one - it'll be much easier for reviewers.
good call, splitting into 3 prs then. should i rebase each onto latest dev first or just let the pr diff show as is

a quick `git fetch && git merge origin/dev` on each before opening is worth it, just to catch any new conflicts before a reviewer sees them - the shared-branch caveat from earlier doesn't apply here since these would be solo feature branches nobody else has fetched.
makes sense, will do that for each one before opening. thanks for all the help this sprint
good sprint - report feature shipped, a real pagination bug caught and fixed, and the notification badge fix too. good luck with reviews.
